question: Does additional reasoning without supplied constraints improve candidate choices beyond the existing CoC-only condition?
role: Supplementary action-selection controls; not an autonomous-driving system benchmark or an equal-information superiority experiment

methods.name: Zero-shot CoT
methods.procedure: Generate reasoning using the original cot_trigger_no=1, then extract a final answer in a second generation

methods.name: Plan-and-Solve
methods.procedure: Use original basic PS prompt_201 for planning and solving, following the official answer-extraction procedure; no PS+ substitutions or self-consistency

checkpoints: Reuse the existing P0 final LoRA checkpoint for each task family and optimization seed
failure_accounting: Invalid outputs remain in the denominator; report their frequency separately and do not invent an action label or an admissibility verdict
budget_accounting: Original code defaults give unequal reasoning token caps; report actual cost and do not claim equal inference budgets
interpretation_limits: Both methods are transferred prompting procedures on our VLM and dataset, not full reproductions of their original GPT-3 experiments
Neither is a driving-specific model or a replacement reproduction of DriveLM/DriveVLM
Current paired data contain identical P0 image-and-prompt inputs with different targets; the best fixed output per identical input is correct on at most 50 percent of the rows
More reasoning cannot recover an omitted experimental rule; differences from P2 mix information availability and reasoning strategy
Reusing P0 checkpoints tests inference procedures, not new training methods or training-only gains
reporting_gate: Keep these controls supplementary. Do not add numerical claims or graphs before full inference and scoring are actually complete.
